per_case_metrics.name: Logic Regression: Off-by-one in Pagination Slicing

findings.label: issue
findings.subject: Off-by-one in pagination slice drops one item per page
findings.description: The slice end was changed from offset + page_size to offset + page_size - 1. As a result, each page returns at most page_size - 1 items. For page_size == 1, every page returns an empty list. For page_size > 1, the last item of each page is omitted, and since offset is still computed as (page - 1) * page_size, the omitted item is never returned on any page, silently losing data. Callers relying on full pages (e.g., UI grids, batch processing) will see short pages and missing records.
findings.suggested_action: Revert the slice end to offset + page_size: `return list(items[offset : offset + page_size])`. If a different page size semantics is intended, adjust offset and page_size consistently and add tests covering page_size == 1, boundary pages, and last partial page.

findings.label: issue
findings.subject: Non-constant-time signature comparison enables timing attacks
findings.description: The computed HMAC digest is compared to the attacker-supplied `expected_sig` using Python's `==` operator. String equality short-circuits on the first mismatched byte, so comparison time varies with the number of matching leading bytes. An attacker who can submit many webhook requests and measure response timing can recover a valid signature byte-by-byte, bypassing signature validation.
findings.suggested_action: Use `hmac.compare_digest(computed, expected_sig)` for the comparison. Also consider validating that `expected_sig` is a well-formed hex string of the expected length before comparing.
